digest: src/ has 3 TypeScript files covering stop, cancellation, and terminal summary; no test files exist in the repo, and store.js/types.js are absent.

implementationMap.observedBehavior: createWorkflowStopSignal polls every 200ms by default and clamps pollMs to a minimum of 1ms. It does not match the spec's 50ms default and 10ms floor.

implementationMap.evidence: const intent = await readWorkflowStopIntent(cwd, runId).catch(() => undefined);
implementationMap.observedBehavior: Read failures in the watcher path are swallowed and treated as no stop intent, which matches S4 for that path.

implementationMap.evidence: export async function throwIfWorkflowStopRequested(...) { ... const intent = await readWorkflowStopIntent(cwd, runId);
implementationMap.observedBehavior: Read errors are not caught here, so they propagate to the caller as S4 requires.

dispose clears the interval, so no new ticks start. check() only guards on controller.signal.aborted at entry, and an already in-flight read can still call abort after dispose. Whether this breaks S5 depends on the reading of S5.
isWorkflowStopRequestedError also returns true on a message prefix match, so it does not satisfy S6 as written, which forbids message-based detection.

implementationMap.evidence:
export function workflowStopRequestedMessage(runId: string): string {
	return `workflow stop requested for ${runId}`;
implementationMap.observedBehavior: createWorkflowStopRequestedError sets name WorkflowStopRequested and the message matches the S2 format.
bindWorkflowLaunchSignal returns an unbind function. The unbind removes the Set entry when empty and checks the map identity before deleting. This appears to match S7, but no test covers it.

implementationMap.component: Stop intent detection (disk or foreground signal)
implementationMap.observedBehavior: Stop is detected from either a disk intent or an aborted launch signal keyed on workflowRunPath(cwd, runId), which matches S1 in shape.

implementationMap.evidence: if (candidate === "aborted" || candidate === "AbortError" || candidate === "ABORT_ERR" || candidate === "cancelled" || candidate === "timeout") return true;
implementationMap.observedBehavior: The error/reason check accepts "cancelled" and "timeout" as cancellation in addition to the three values in C1, so it exceeds the exact set C1 allows.

implementationMap.evidence:
if (value.cancelled === true) return true;
		const details = ...; if (details?.cancelled === true) return true;
implementationMap.observedBehavior: Boolean cancelled flags on the value or details also count as cancellation. C1 covers only error/reason strings, so this is an extra path to review.

Recursion into parsed content text is guarded only by a self-identity check (parsed !== value). Chains of distinct JSON strings are not depth-bounded, so C2's no-infinite-recursion requirement needs a closer look.

implementationMap.evidence:
if (typeof DOMException !== "undefined" && value instanceof DOMException)
			return value.name === "AbortError";
implementationMap.observedBehavior: isWorkflowAbortError accepts a DOMException or record whose name is AbortError, which is consistent with C1's AbortError value.

implementationMap.component: Terminal semantic status for non-dynamic runs
implementationMap.observedBehavior: A completed run with a degradation record maps to completed_degraded, matching T1.

implementationMap.component: Terminal semantic status for direct-dynamic runs
implementationMap.observedBehavior: When control.json cannot be read, control is undefined and the status falls through to completed_without_semantic_result, which matches T2 provided the run reaches that branch. The check runs only when terminal and mode is direct-dynamic.

outputRetryAttempts sums outputRetry.attempts across tasks. The launch-retry total is exposed as launchRetries, not launchRetryAttempts. T3 names the public field launchRetryAttempts, so the field name differs from the spec.
Controller task is found by spec id or status detail, and control.json is read from the directory of the task output path.

implementationMap.evidence: Glob for *.test.* and test/tests/__tests__/spec directories returned no files; package.json scripts only define typecheck.
implementationMap.observedBehavior: No unit tests exist in the repository for any S, C, or T item, so Q1 has no evidence in the repository.

unmappedAreas: store.js (readWorkflowStopIntent, workflowRunPath, readJson, finalStageTasks, fromProjectPath, isTerminalWorkflowStatus) is absent, so the stop-intent read path and run-path keying cannot be verified
types.js (WorkflowRunRecord) is absent, so field shapes such as degradation, outputRetry, and launchRetry cannot be confirmed
probe/ directory is untracked and was not reviewed as implementation
tests for S7 unbind and T2 fallback behavior were not located anywhere in the repository
notes: Spec review baseline: SPEC.md at repo root. Conformance is not decided here; only mapped evidence is recorded.

Mismatches observed for later verification: S3 defaults (200ms, floor 1ms vs 50ms/10ms), S6 message-prefix fallback, C1 extra accepted strings (cancelled, timeout) and boolean flags, T3 field name launchRetries vs launchRetryAttempts.
Recent git commit 654f639 touched stop polling and timeout cancellation, which may explain the drift from spec values.
